DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Brain Tumor (likely Glioblastoma or Meningioma) with potential cerebral edema causing visual field deficits.

The clinical picture of a 69-year-old with a progressive headache and worsening vision over three weeks, in the absence of fever or weight loss, strongly suggests an intracranial mass lesion rather than an infectious or systemic metabolic cause. I am requesting neuroimaging to confirm the location and nature of the lesion.

REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI with contrast.
